results.title: Fix PyTorch mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied — tensorViz
results.content:
Save the files below in one folder. The models use random initial weights and synthetic inputs; they do not download a dataset or checkpoint.

broken.py ↓ fixed.py ↓ pooled.py ↓ verify.py ↓ requirements.txt ↓

From that folder, run:

```
python verify.py
```

 Need a separate environment?

For macOS or Linux with Python 3.12 available, these commands create a separate environment and install the tested PyTorch pin. Keep your existing project's Torch/CUDA setup unchanged.

```
python3.12 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python verify.py
```

The script catches the deliberate errors, checks the corrections, and finishes with `All CPU checks passed. Fix the feature contract; do not reshape away the mismatch.` Here is the broken model: [...] Do not copy 512 into every model. It follows from this model’s channels and spatial size. Replacing a trained Linear layer also changes its parameter shape; an old 128-feature head cannot be loaded directly into the new 512-feature head.

04 / KEEP THE BATCH INTACT

## A reshape can hide the error and break the model.

The tempting workaround is `x.reshape(-1, 128)`. Our two flattened images contain `2  512 = 1024` values, so that expression produces `[8, 128]`. The broken head now runs and returns `[8, 5]`: eight predictions for two images. [...] Shapes from the CPU example, with batch size 2

| Stage | Shape | What changed |
| Input images | `[2, 3, 16, 16]` | Batch, channels, height, width |
| Features after MaxPool2d | `[2, 8, 8, 8]` | 8 channels, 8 × 8 spatial values |
| Flatten(start\_dim=1) | `[2, 512]` | 512 features for each image |
| Broken Linear head | `512 → expects 128` | The forward call fails here |

The convolution keeps the spatial size because its 3 × 3 kernel uses padding 1. The 2 × 2 pooling reduces 16 × 16 to 8 × 8. Flattening from dimension 1 keeps the batch dimension and combines the remaining dimensions: `8  8  8 = 512`.

### About

tensorViz helps developers explore PyTorch models and JAX/Flax programs as interactive graphs. For PyTorch, users can expand nested modules, inspect tensor shapes captured from one forward pass, jump to Python source, and review architecture changes beside code diffs. The website offers recorded model graphs to explore without installation. The free VS Code extension is available from the Visual Studio Marketplace and Open VSX. Local capture requires Python, model dependencies, and example inputs. Standalone coding-agent plugins are an Apple Silicon macOS preview; MCP agents can also connect to the extension. JAX/Flax graphs use CPU tracing with inferred shapes, and PyTorch source edits are unavailable for them.

results.title: tensorViz vs Netron vs torchview vs Model Explorer vs TensorBoard — PyTorch model visualization compared
results.content:
tensorViz does not publish a parameter-count limit; one has not been established. Memory, model construction and the forward call still matter.

07 / PICK BY TASK

## When should I use each tool? [...] - Collapse by default. tensorViz shows modules as cards you expand or enter, with a breadcrumb back. Search accepts names (`conv1`), types (`type=Conv2d`) or shapes (`shape=256`). Hits inside a collapsed module stay grouped until you open it. Model Explorer and torchvista also collapse nested layers. torchview limits `depth`.
- Avoid allocating real tensors. torchview accepts `device='meta'`. tensorViz has an experimental `fake` or `auto` trace tier that records shapes without tensor data. It retries once with real tensors if the model needs values. The default is real tensors. [...] | See an interactive graph inside a Jupyter or Colab cell | torchvista | Built for web-based notebooks. tensorViz has no documented notebook integration. |
| Debug gradients or see what autograd saves | torchviz | `make_dot` draws the backward graph, with `show_saved=True` |
| Explore your own `nn.Module` beside its Python, with shapes, and go from a layer to its source | tensorViz | An editor extension with code focus. No export step. |
| Let a coding agent open and discuss the model graph | tensorViz | A plugin for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, and MCP from the extension |
| Review how an architecture changed in a diff or pull request | tensorViz | Review model changes; diff a PyTorch model between git commits compares source review with rendering each revision separately. |
